name: Mystery in Nature: Fascination and Likeability of Trail Scenes
description: Faithful replication of the rating task with the original images: participants rate 80 nature-trail photographs, 40 normed as high in mystery and 40 as low in mystery. They come in two blocks of 40 (20 of each kind, random order within each block) with a break between. Each trial shows a fixation cross for 2 s and the photo for 5 s, then two questionnaires in random order: the three-item fascination subscale of the Shortened Perceived Restorativeness Scale (0 = not at all to 6 = very much so) and a single likeability item (1 = a strong dislike to 7 = a strong preference). Age and gender are asked at the end. Rebuilt from Marois, Charbonneau, Szolosi & Watson (2021), Frontiers in Psychology 12: 759616; the images are the stimulus set of Szolosi, Watson & Ruddell (2014), Frontiers in Psychology 5: 1360, released in its Data Sheets 3-4 under CC BY 4.0, together with per-image mystery and fascination norms (stored in this template). Analysis as in the paper: average the three fascination items per image and participant, then compare high- and low-mystery images with paired t-tests on fascination and on likeability; per-image means can be correlated with the 2014 norms. Differences from the original study: (1) no eye tracking (the paper's main measures were pupil size, fixations and saccades); (2) online rather than in a dimly lit lab with headphones; (3) photos are split into the two blocks at random per participant, so block order is counterbalanced by randomisation rather than by fixed sets; (4) the likeability question wording and the gender options are ours (the paper gives only the scale anchors); (5) the paper's sociodemographic survey is reduced to age and gender.
author: Marois, Charbonneau, Szolosi & Watson

elements.title: I agree to take part. Participation is voluntary and my answers are recorded anonymously for research.

elements.name: fascination

rows.text: This place has qualities that fascinate me.
I would like to spend more time looking at the surroundings here.
My attention is drawn to many interesting things here.

elements.title: To what extent does each statement describe the experience you were having while looking at the image? (0 = not at all, 6 = very much so)
elements.description: Fascination subscale of the Shortened Perceived Restorativeness Scale, three items as quoted in the paper, 0-6. Perceived fascination = mean of f1-f3. Keyed by image id (0_N = low mystery, 1_N = high mystery).

elements.name: liking
elements.title: How much did you like the image you have just seen?
elements.description: Likeability scale, 1 = a strong dislike to 7 = a strong preference (anchors from the paper; question wording is ours). Keyed by image id.
